key_insight: ACCESS decouples finding good solutions from checking feasibility in chance-constrained optimization, using cheap single-scenario search followed by large-scale simulation-based validation.
engineering_relevance: This makes stochastic design under uncertainty more scalable on modern hardware, especially when feasibility checks can be massively parallelized on GPUs.
method: Generate many candidate solutions from inexpensive single-scenario subproblems instead of full SAA over the whole uncertain model.
Evaluate candidate feasibility separately with batched simulation over a very large number of scenarios.
Use a 2D control space for conservatism and scenario diversity; ACCESS(δ) adds certified feasibility with probability 1-δ.
evidence_signal: Across three benchmark classes and five scenario distributions, ACCESS matched or beat the best objective in nearly every setting, while ACCESS(δ) was empirically feasible on every instance and SAA was often infeasible and much slower.
watch_item: The framework depends on strong simulation throughput and careful tuning of conservatism/diversity, so performance may vary if scenario sampling is unrepresentative or GPU resources are limited.
paper_title: Optimization for One, Feasibility for Most: Decoupling Optimization from Feasibility in Chance-Constrained Programs
